definitions: To place in or on a rack.
To cause extreme pain, distress, or anguish to.
To strain or exert to the utmost.
To draw off (wine or liquor) from the lees.
To hit (a ball) into a pocket in billiards or pool.
examples: She began to rack the dishes.
The illness began to rack his body.
He began to rack his brains for an answer.
They began to rack the wine.
He began to rack the eight ball.
